## Closer Look at Credit Ratings for CDOs

Rama CONT

Amal MOUSSA

## Dept of Statistics Center for Financial Engineering Columbia University; New York

Laboratoire de Probabiltés et Modèles Aléatoires; CNRS (Paris)

## Abstract

ucts have played an important role in the development of the structured credit market, which has been cast into the limelight by the recent credit crisis. This study aims at clarifying some misconceptions related to CDO ratings; their interpretation and their use\_ prod-

We first  describe the rating  approaches   used by major agencies   for CDOs and other structured credit products. Most rating agencies have been using static factor models which are slight variations on the Gaussian copula model allowing for intersector and intrasector correlations. this framework, we explore several issues related to CDO as follows: Using ratings

Our findings can be summarized

- Given the leveraged nature of CDOs; the downgrade risk of CDO tranche can be quite different bond with same initial rating. Therefore; simple labeling via default probability or expected loss not discriminate sufficiently their downgrade risk. from does
- CDO tranche ratings require assumptions on the dependence structure of the default times and are thus exposed to model risk. We explore this model risk for CDO and CDO-squared tranches in multisector factor model.
- The interaction between the rating threshold and the structuring procedure can cause new issues to have tranches structured at the limit" of rating categories and thus a high probability of downgrading
- Migration probabilities for tranches with similar can vary from structure to structure even for the same underlying debt portfolio: two tranches with the same can have   completely different transition probabilities\_ rating rating

The paper will be presented by Amal Moussa.  Email: am2810@columbia.edu
